pages.text: Faisal loves football, but he is the smallest boy in his class. At break time, nobody picks him for a team.
"You're too small," says Omar. Faisal sits on a bench and watches the game. He is sad, but he doesn't go home.
On Thursday, there is a big match against another school. But Majed, the goalkeeper, is ill. "Who can catch the ball?" asks the teacher.
Faisal puts up his hand. "I can! I catch my brother's ball every day in the garden." Omar laughs, but the teacher says, "OK, Faisal. Get your gloves!"
The score is one-one. In the last minute, a tall boy kicks the ball very hard. Faisal jumps high and catches it!
Everyone shouts and claps. Omar runs to him and says, "Sorry, Faisal. You're small, but you're the best!" Faisal smiles. "Can I play with you at break time tomorrow?" "Of course!" says Omar.

pages.text: Layla and her grandpa made a robot. Its name was Tiko. Tiko had big round eyes, and they could shine like lamps.
"Tiko can't run or jump," said Layla's brother, Faisal. "He's very slow!" Tiko moved his arms and said, "Beep. I am sorry."
On Thursday, they took Tiko to the school science fair. There were robots that could dance, sing and play football. Layla felt sad.
Then suddenly, all the lights went out. It was very dark, and a little boy started to cry. "Where's my mum?" he shouted.
"Tiko, eyes on!" said Layla. Tiko's eyes shone bright yellow, and slowly he walked to the boy. Now everyone could see, and the boy found his mum.
The teacher gave Tiko a gold star. Faisal smiled. "Slow is OK. Tiko is the best robot here!"

pages.text: Faisal and his grandmother walked in old Jeddah. The houses were tall and very old. "This street is two hundred years old," Grandma said.
Grandma stopped at a big green door. She took an old key out of her bag. "I lived here when I was a girl," she said.
The key was heavy, and the door opened slowly. Inside, it was dark and quiet. Faisal saw beautiful wooden windows.
"Where did you sleep, Grandma?" asked Faisal. "Up those stairs," she said. "Come, I want to show you something."
In a small room, Grandma touched the wall. There were old letters on it: "Huda, 10 years old." "I wrote that sixty years ago!" she laughed.
Faisal took a small stone from the floor. He wrote under her name: "Faisal, 9 years old." "Now this house has our story too," Grandma said with a smile.

pages.text: Omar and his family went to the beach by the Red Sea. At night, the moon was big and white. "Look! Something is moving in the sand!" said his sister, Lina.
They were baby turtles! They were very small and had tiny flippers. But the turtles walked away from the sea.
"Why are they going the wrong way?" asked Omar. Dad pointed to the bright lights of the café. "They think the lights are the moon on the water," he said.
Omar ran to the café. "Please turn off the lights for ten minutes!" he said. The man smiled and turned them off.
Now the beach was dark, and the moon shone on the sea. The baby turtles turned around. They walked quickly to the water.
One small turtle stopped and looked back. "Goodbye, little friend!" said Lina. Then a wave came, and the turtle swam away into the big, blue sea.

pages.text: Every Friday, Grandma makes date cakes, and they are the best cakes in the family. "What's your secret, Grandma?" asks Lina.
Grandma smiles and holds up a small blue box. "My secret is in here," she says, but she never opens it.
One Friday, Grandma is sick in bed, and the cousins are coming for lunch. "Oh no! No date cakes today!" cries Omar, but Lina says, "Don't worry, I can make them!"
Lina mixes flour, butter, eggs and dates, and she bakes the cakes in the oven. They look beautiful, but they taste wrong. Something is missing!
Lina runs to Grandma's room, and Grandma gives her the blue box. Inside, there is a brown powder with a wonderful smell. "It's cardamom, just one small spoon!" says Grandma.
Lina makes the cakes again, and the family eats every one. "These are Grandma's cakes!" says Omar. Grandma laughs and says, "No, now they are Lina's cakes."

pages.text: Lina loved music. Every morning, she sang in the garden with the birds. "One day, I want to play in a concert," she said.
"Next week, we have a school concert," said her teacher. "Bring an instrument!" But Lina didn't have a drum or a guitar, and she felt sad.
At home, Grandpa hit his glass with a spoon. Ding! "Listen, Lina," he said. "Water can sing too!"
They put seven bottles on the table. Some bottles had a lot of water, and some had a little. Each bottle made a different sound.
Lina practised every evening after her homework. Her little brother danced and laughed. Soon she could play a whole song.
At the concert, everyone looked at the bottles and smiled. Then Lina played, and the room was very quiet. At the end, everyone clapped, and Grandpa clapped the loudest!

stories.title: The Case of the Missing Hat

pages.text: "Where is my white hat?" asked Grandpa at the desert camp. "It was on this chair!" Sara and Omar took out their notebook and said, "Don't worry, Grandpa. We are detectives!"
Next to the chair, Omar saw big round footprints in the sand. "Look! These are not people's feet," he said. "They are very, very big!"
Then Sara found small pieces of dry grass on the chair. "Who eats grass?" she asked. "Goats eat grass," said Omar, and he wrote it in the notebook.
They followed the footprints behind the big tent. The goats were asleep there, and their feet were very small. "It isn't the goats," said Sara. "The footprints don't stop here!"
Then they heard a funny noise behind a palm tree. It was Noura, Grandpa's camel! She had the white hat on her head, and she looked very happy.
Everyone laughed, and Grandpa laughed the loudest. "Case closed!" said Sara. Grandpa gave his two clever detectives sweet dates and a big hug.

pages.text: Faisal loves superheroes, and he draws them every day in his big blue book. "I want a superpower too!" he says to his grandpa.
Grandpa smiles. "You have one, Faisal. You see small things that other people don't see." Faisal laughs. "That's not a superpower, Grandpa!"
On Friday, Faisal and Grandpa go to the park. Faisal hears a little boy crying under a tree. "I can't find my mum," says the boy. "She has a yellow bag."
Faisal looks and looks. There are many people and many bags in the park. Then he sees something yellow behind the tall trees, next to the shop.
A woman with a yellow bag is calling, "Yusuf! Yusuf!" The little boy runs to his mum, and she hugs him. "Thank you, Faisal!" she says.
That night, Faisal opens his blue book and draws a new superhero with very big eyes. He writes a name under it: SUPER EYES. Grandpa smiles. "Now you know your superpower!"

pages.text: Omar and his family went camping in the desert. Dad put up a big tent near the rocks. Omar's sister, Huda, carried the blankets.
At night, they sat by the fire and ate dates. "Look at the stars!" said Huda. "There are hundreds!"
Later, Omar heard a sound outside the tent. Scratch, scratch! "What's that?" whispered Huda.
Omar took his torch and looked outside. Something small and round was next to the bag of dates. It was brown, and it had lots of sharp spikes!
"It's a hedgehog!" laughed Omar. "It's hungry, like us." Huda put a date on a rock for it.
In the morning, the date wasn't there. Next to the rock, there were tiny footprints in the sand. "Our first camping friend!" Dad said with a smile.

pages.text: On Sunday morning, Omar ran into his classroom. The class tortoise, Speedy, lived in a big box by the window. But today, the box was empty!
"Where is Speedy?" Omar shouted. Mr. Khalid looked under every desk. "Tortoises are very slow, so he can't be far," he said.
The boys looked in the library and in the playground. Faisal checked behind the big bookcase. But they couldn't find Speedy anywhere.
Back in the classroom, Omar heard a quiet sound: crunch, crunch, crunch! It came from Yusuf's school bag. The bag was on the floor next to Speedy's box.
Yusuf opened his bag slowly. There was Speedy, eating Yusuf's lettuce sandwich! Everyone laughed, and Yusuf laughed the loudest.
"Speedy isn't slow when he is hungry!" said Mr. Khalid. That afternoon, the class made a strong new lid for the box. Now Yusuf brings an extra piece of lettuce every day, just for Speedy.

pages.text: On Friday, my family went to the desert. Dad put up a big tent, and Mum made hot tea. My little brother Fahad played in the sand.
Then Grandma looked around. "Where is Fahad?" she asked. We called his name, but there was no answer.
Dad took his torch, and I held Grandma's hand. We walked up a big hill of sand. The wind was cold, and the sun went down.
Then I saw small footprints in the sand. "Look, Dad! Fahad went this way!" I shouted. We followed them quickly.
Behind a tree, we found Fahad. He was next to a mother camel and her baby! "The baby is hungry," Fahad said, and he gave it his bread.
Dad laughed and picked Fahad up. "Next time, you must stay with your family," Grandma said with a smile. Back at the tent, we all drank tea under the bright stars.

pages.text: Sara has a small robot. Its name is Zoom. Zoom is round, and it cleans the floor every morning.
One day, Grandma was sad. "I can't find my gold ring!" she said. Everyone looked under the chairs and tables.
Sara had an idea. "Zoom has a camera," she said. "It can go under the sofa!"
Zoom went under the big sofa. Sara watched on her tablet. It was very dark, but then something was shining.
"Stop, Zoom!" Sara shouted. Dad moved the sofa. There was Grandma's ring, next to an old toy car!
Grandma smiled and hugged Sara. "Thank you, clever girl! And thank you, Zoom!" Zoom beeped happily.

stories.title: The Man in the Dark Room

pages.text: A long time ago, a clever man lived in Cairo. His name was Ibn al-Haytham. He loved light, and he asked many questions.
"How do our eyes see?" he asked his young helper, Yusuf. "Light comes from the sun," said Yusuf. "Yes, but how does it go into our eyes?"
Ibn al-Haytham went into a very dark room. There was one small hole in the wall. "Come and look, Yusuf!" he called.
On the wall, there was a picture of the street outside! Yusuf saw a camel and a tree. "But the camel is upside down!" he laughed.
"Light moves in straight lines," said Ibn al-Haytham. "It comes through the hole and makes a picture. Our eyes work like this room."
Yusuf smiled. "You are a hero of light!" Ibn al-Haytham wrote many books about light. Today, every camera works like his dark room.

He helped people understand light and how we see

pages.text: It is a hot day in the desert. Omar and his sister Lina are at Grandpa's farm. The sky is blue, and the sun is very strong.
Suddenly, Lina points. "Look, Omar! The sky is orange!" A big wall of sand is coming fast.
"It's a sandstorm!" says Grandpa. "Quick! Bring the goats into the barn!" Omar runs to the goats, and Lina closes the gate.
Now they are in the house. The wind is loud, and the windows are shaking. Omar counts the goats in his head. "Oh no! The baby goat is missing!"
Then they hear a small sound. "Baa!" The baby goat is under the kitchen table! "He is scared of the wind too," says Lina, and everyone laughs.
After an hour, the wind stops. Then it starts to rain! Grandpa smiles. "First sand, then rain. That is desert weather!"

pages.text: Omar loved painting. On Sunday, there was an art competition at his school. He wanted to paint the desert.
He painted yellow sand and a big blue sky. Then he added a brown camel. "It's finished!" he said.
His little sister Huda ran into the room. Oh no! She dropped a cup of water on the painting.
The red, yellow and blue paint ran together. Omar was very sad. "My picture is wrong now!" he cried.
Huda looked at the painting carefully. "Look, Omar! The sky is orange and pink now. It's an evening sky!"
At school, the teacher smiled. "What a beautiful sunset!" she said. Omar won first prize, and he hugged Huda. "Thank you! You're an artist too!"

pages.text: Noor found an old clock in Grandpa's room. It had a small gold key. She turned the key, and the room went round and round!
Now Noor was in a village with no cars. A boy sat next to a little house. "I want a tree, but I have only one seed," he said.
"Let's plant it together!" said Noor. They dug a hole and gave the seed some water. "Thank you! My name is Saad," said the boy.
Then the clock went tick, tick, tick. Noor waved goodbye to Saad. The room went round and round again.
Noor ran outside to Grandpa Saad. There was a big palm tree in the garden. "I planted this tree with a girl a long time ago," Grandpa said.
"She had a clock like yours," he laughed. Noor smiled and gave him a sweet date from the tree. "Thank you, my old friend," she said.

pages.text: Faisal and his sister Noura went to the beach in Jeddah with Dad. The sea was blue and the sand was hot. But there was a lot of rubbish on the sand.
"Look!" shouted Noura. "Something is moving in that plastic bag!" They ran to it quickly.
It was a small sea turtle. It couldn't swim because the bag was around its leg. "Be careful," said Dad.
Faisal held the turtle gently. Noura took the bag off its leg. The turtle opened its eyes and looked at them.
They put the turtle near the water. It walked slowly into the waves and swam away. "Goodbye, little friend!" Noura laughed.
Then Faisal had an idea. "Let's clean the beach for all the turtles!" They picked up bottles and bags all afternoon, and Dad was very proud.

pages.text: Every morning, Mr. Saleh stood at the school gate. He smiled and said, "Good morning!" to every student. But there was no shade, and the sun was very hot.
One day, Huda saw Mr. Saleh's red face. "He's hot and tired," she said to her friend Noura. "Let's help him!"
At break time, the girls told their teacher, Miss Amal. "What a good idea!" she said. "The whole class can help."
The next day, everyone brought something. Huda brought a big green umbrella, and Noura brought a cold bottle of water. The other girls made a card with a picture of a smiling sun.
In the morning, the class ran to the gate. "Surprise!" they shouted. Mr. Saleh opened the card, and his eyes were wet with happy tears.
"Thank you, my daughters," he said. On Thursday, he brought a big box of sweet dates for the whole class. "Kindness is like a ball," Huda laughed. "When you throw it, it comes back to you!"

pages.text: Omar and his grandfather camped in the desert. At night, Omar went to say goodnight to Nour, the baby camel. But Nour was not there!
"Grandpa, Nour is lost!" Omar shouted. Grandpa took his torch, and Omar took a bottle of water. "Come on, let's find her," said Grandpa.
They followed small footprints in the sand. Then the wind blew hard, and the footprints were gone. "What can we do now?" Omar asked quietly.
Grandpa looked up at the sky. "Look at that bright star. Camels often walk to the old rocks under it."
They walked to a big hill with old rocks. Omar heard a sad, soft sound behind a rock. It was Nour, and her leg was stuck between two stones!
Omar moved the stones carefully, and Nour stood up. Omar gave her some water, and they walked back to the tent. "You were very brave tonight," Grandpa said, and Omar smiled at the star.

pages.text: Omar lives near the desert with his grandfather. They have ten camels. The smallest camel is Noor, and she loves Omar's whistle.
One afternoon, the wind was very strong. Sand flew everywhere, and everyone ran inside. "Where is Noor?" Omar shouted.
When the wind stopped, Omar and Grandpa looked for her. They looked behind the tents and next to the water. But Noor wasn't there.
"Camels can walk a long way," Grandpa said sadly. Then Omar had an idea. He climbed a tall sand hill and whistled loudly.
They waited and waited. Then they heard a quiet sound from behind the big rocks. Noor ran up the hill to Omar!
That night, Noor drank warm milk next to Omar. "You're a clever boy," Grandpa smiled. "No, Grandpa," Omar laughed. "Noor is the clever one. She listened!"

After dinner, Noor and Grandpa go up to the roof with a telescope. The sky is dark and full of stars.
"Look, Grandpa, that star is moving!" says Noor. Grandpa smiles and says, "It's not a star. It's the space station."
"Is Aunt Huda in there?" asks Noor. "Yes, she is," says Grandpa. Noor jumps up and waves.
The bright light goes across the sky, and then it is gone. Noor feels a little sad. "Can she see me?" she asks.
The next morning, Aunt Huda calls on the phone. "I saw the lights of your city last night," she says. "I waved to you, Noor!"

stories.title: The Slow Boy in the Goal

pages.text: Yusuf loves football, but he is not fast. In every game, the other boys run past him. "Never mind," says his grandfather. "Try something different."
On Friday, the school team has a big match. Their goalkeeper, Sami, is ill. "Who can stand in the goal?" asks Coach Khalid.
Nobody answers. Then Yusuf puts up his hand. "I can't run fast, but I can catch!" he says.
The match starts. The other team kicks the ball again and again. Yusuf jumps and catches it every time.
It is the last minute, and the score is one-one. A tall boy kicks the ball very hard. Yusuf flies to the left and stops it!
Then Yusuf throws the ball far to Ali, and Ali scores. Everyone shouts, "Yusuf! Yusuf!" Now he has a new place on the team.

pages.text: Mum's silver ring was on the kitchen table. In the morning, it wasn't there! "Where is my ring?" Mum asked.
The next day, Dad's car key went missing. Then Omar's new spoon went too. "Who is taking our shiny things?" said Omar.
Omar and his sister Lina looked for clues. They found a small black feather by the open window. "A feather!" said Lina.
The children waited quietly near the window. Suddenly, a black bird flew into the kitchen! It took a shiny button and flew to the palm tree.
Dad got a ladder and climbed up the tree. In the bird's nest, he found the ring, the key and the spoon! "Here is our thief," he laughed.
Mum was very happy to have her ring again. Lina put an old shiny button in the nest. "That's for you, Mr Bird!" she said.

pages.text: Yusuf and Adam were at the beach in Jeddah. They wanted to build the biggest sandcastle in the world. "Let's start!" said Adam.
Yusuf made a tall tower, and Adam made a long wall. "My tower is the best!" said Yusuf. "No, my wall is better!" shouted Adam.
The boys stopped talking. Yusuf sat on one side, and Adam sat on the other side. Then Adam saw a very big wave.
"Yusuf, quick! Help me!" Adam called. They put sand on the wall together, fast, fast, fast! But the water came over the wall.
The tower fell down into the water. The boys looked at each other. Then they laughed and laughed.
"Let's build it again," said Yusuf. "Together this time!" At sunset, their castle was the biggest on the beach.

stories.title: The Magic of the Sun Plate

pages.text: Omar washed the yard with Grandpa. There was a big puddle near the door. After lunch, the puddle was gone!
"Where did the water go?" asked Omar. Grandpa smiled. "Let's do a test and find out."
Grandpa put salty water on two plates. One plate went in the hot sun. The other plate went in the dark kitchen.
Omar checked the plates every hour. The sun plate got drier and drier. The kitchen plate was still wet.
In the evening, the sun plate had no water, but there was white salt on it! "The sun took the water up into the air," said Grandpa.
"The water goes up, but the salt stays!" said Omar. That night, Mum put Omar's salt on the salad. "Science tastes good!" Omar laughed.

pages.text: Faisal and his grandpa drove into the desert. They wanted to see the stars. The sand was gold, and the sky was very big.
At night, the car stopped. "Grandpa, the car is broken!" said Faisal. His phone didn't work, too.
Grandpa smiled. "Don't be afraid. The stars can help us." He pointed to a very bright star.
"That star shows us the north. Our camp is north," said Grandpa. They walked slowly over the cold sand.
Then Faisal heard a sound. It was a camel! Behind it, he saw a small fire and a tent.
"You found us!" shouted Uncle Khalid. They drank hot milk by the fire. Faisal looked up and said quietly, "Thank you, stars."

One afternoon, Kiwi shouted, "Dinner is ready!" Dad ran to the kitchen. Omar and his sister ran too.
But the table was empty. Mum laughed and said, "I didn't say that. Kiwi did!"
The next day, Kiwi shouted, "Omar! Do your homework!" Omar sat down and opened his book. Then he saw Kiwi's funny face and laughed.
In the evening, Mum called, "Dinner is ready!" Nobody came. "It's Kiwi again," Dad said with a smile.

pages.text: Noura and her grandfather went out on his small boat. The Red Sea was blue and quiet. 'Look for dolphins!' Grandpa said.

'Grandpa, help!' Noura shouted. Grandpa stopped the boat. He took his small knife and moved slowly to the turtle.
'Be careful!' said Noura. Grandpa cut the net, piece by piece. The turtle was tired, but it moved its legs again.
The turtle swam around the boat one time. Then it looked at Noura with its dark eyes. 'It's saying thank you!' she laughed.
Noura put the old net in a bag. 'Now it can't hurt more animals,' she said. Just then, two dolphins jumped next to the boat, and Grandpa smiled.

pages.text: Noura loves building things. Her grandpa has a small garden with tomatoes. Every day, he carries heavy water to the plants.

Mum helped her make small holes in the bottles. Then Noura filled them with water. She put them upside down in the ground next to the plants.
Her brother Fahad laughed. "Bottles can't water plants!" But the next morning, the ground was wet and the leaves were green.
Grandpa smiled. "The water comes out slowly, drop by drop," he said. "You made rain under the ground!"

pages.text: Grandpa showed Omar an old photo. "This is me at Elephant Rock. I was ten." Omar said, "I'm ten too! Can we go there?"
The family drove to AlUla. The desert was big and orange. Omar looked out of the window all day.
At night, they slept in a tent. The sky was full of stars. "Tomorrow we find the elephant," Grandpa said.
In the morning, they walked between tall rocks. "Is that the elephant?" asked Omar's sister, Lina. "No!" laughed Omar. "That rock looks like a camel!"
Then Omar saw a giant rock with a long nose. "There it is!" he shouted. Grandpa smiled. "It's bigger than I remember."
Omar stood in the same place as Grandpa in the old photo. Dad took a new photo. Now the family had two photos: Grandpa at ten and Omar at ten.
